statement: Build a one-page website for Brew Lab, a cafe in Indiranagar, Bengaluru, that shows its menu with prices, opening hours, location and phone number, a photo gallery with empty spots, and stories about where its coffee comes from.
audience: People in and around Bengaluru deciding whether to visit Brew Lab, and regulars checking the menu, hours or address, mostly on their phones.
standards: Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript in one file, no build step
Readable and usable on a phone (360px wide) and a desktop (1280px wide) with no sideways scrolling
All text is real content from the Requester; no invented facts, photos, reviews or links
Warm, simple look that suits a specialty coffee cafe
rules: Use only the facts the Requester supplied: address, hours, phone, menu items and prices, and the three coffee stories
Do not invent an email, Instagram page, map link or opening-day exceptions
Do not use stock or placeholder photos as if they were the cafe's own; gallery spots stay clearly empty
Prices are shown in rupees exactly as given
done_when: The page shows the name Brew Lab and says it is a cafe in Bengaluru
A menu section lists exactly: Espresso ₹120, Cappuccino ₹180, Cold brew ₹200, Pour-over ₹220, Croissant ₹150, Banana bread ₹130
A timings section states open 8am to 10pm every day, with no closed days
A location section shows the address 100 Feet Road, Indiranagar, Bengaluru 560038
The phone number +91 80 4000 2468 appears on the page as a tap-to-call link
A photo gallery section contains empty, clearly labelled photo spots with no images

A coffee stories section has three stories: Ratnagiri Estate (Chikmagalur, shade-grown coffee), Kerehaklu (Chikmagalur, coffee grown alongside pepper and cardamom), Baarbara Estate (Coorg, only ripe cherries hand-picked)
A navigation menu links to each section and every in-page link points to a section that exists
The page has a mobile viewport setting and layout rules that keep it within the screen width at 360px and 1280px
The page has no JavaScript errors and no text such as 'to be confirmed' or 'lorem ipsum'
